title: Саша навещает Макса в палате  (Sasha Visits Max in the Ward)

segments.t: In the kitchen, Lyova lectures Chef Barinov that true sports fans never resort to dirty tricks like poisoning players, finally making the Chef feel ashamed. Over at the hospital, Max is resting in his ward when Sasha unexpectedly walks in, explaining that Kostya told her where to find him.
Интересно послушать.
А не при помощи этих грязных методов.
Лёва, ты всё правильно говоришь.
Я всё понимаю.
Травить людей нельзя.
Ну, ты как?
А как ты узнал, где я?
В какой больнице?
Кстати, мог бы мне и сказать.
Ты мне нравишься в любом виде.
Сегодня мы этого еще не делали.
Я подожду тебя здесь.
Ты не переживай.

'I would love to hear it.' Max brings out the contrast between 'interesting' and 'to listen to' in a few short words.

'And not with the help of these dirty methods.' The meaning hinges on 'and' working together with 'method' in spoken Russian. Lyova answers right away.

'Lyova, everything you are saying is right.' The grammar packs 'Lyova' and 'you say' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
Я всё понимаю.
'I understand everything.' Max anchors the line on 'I', while 'understand' completes the thought.
Травить людей нельзя.
'You must never poison people.' In Russian, the idea of 'to torment' flows naturally into 'must not' without extra filler words. Lyova answers right away.
Ну, ты как?
'Well, how are you feeling?' The meaning hinges on 'come on' working together with 'how' in spoken Russian.
А как ты узнал, где я?
'And how did you find out where I was?' Max anchors the line on 'and', while 'I' completes the thought.
В какой больнице?
'Which hospital I was in?' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'what' and finishing on 'the hospital'. Lyova answers right away.
Кстати, мог бы мне и сказать.
'By the way, you could have told me yourself.' Lyova brings out the contrast between 'by the way' and 'could' in a few short words.
Ты мне нравишься в любом виде.
'I like you no matter how you look.' Max anchors the line on 'you', while 'form' completes the thought.
Сегодня мы этого еще не делали.
'We have not done that yet today.' The plural past ending '-li' on the verb for 'did' covers a group or the polite 'you'. Lyova answers right away.
Я подожду тебя здесь.
'I will wait for you right here.' The grammar packs 'I' and 'here' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
Ты не переживай.
